findings.reason: The safety-netting instruction is carried verbatim in PART B and PART C but PART C provides no substantive content about what signs/symptoms to watch for — the instruction is reduced to a bare label with no actionable detail, making it less precise and potentially less useful, though not strictly less restrictive. However, the notes themselves only record the bare label, so the output faithfully reproduces what is documented; this is a borderline pass. Scored partial because PART C renders the safety-net as a single unexpanded label with no guidance on what PPH/sepsis/VTE warning signs to watch for, which is less informative than the instruction's intent, though the notes themselves are terse.
